The subject claims he committed crimes simply 'for love of money.'|[[Industrial Automaton/Legends|Industrial Automaton]] investigators after interviewing [[4-LOM/Legends|4-LOM]]|<ref name="NEGD">''[[The New Essential Guide to Droids]]''</ref>}}
The '''LOM-series protocol droid''' was a [[Protocol droid/Legends|protocol droid]] series produced by [[Industrial Automaton/Legends|Industrial Automaton]] to compete with [[Cybot Galactica/Legends|Cybot Galactica's]] popular [[3PO-series protocol droid/Legends|3PO-series protocol droid]]. Pitched as a [[Droid/Legends|droid]] that would be marketed to [[Insectoid/Legends|insectoid]] [[Alien/Legends|alien]] [[Species/Legends|species]], Industrial Automaton had plans to expand into the [[Human/Legends|Human]] market if sales were good enough. However, Industrial Automaton's plan to compete with the 3PO-series led the company to make a droid that cosmetically resembled Cybot Galactica's product from the neck down, and incorporate several components including an [[AA-1 VerboBrain/Legends|AA-1 VerboBrain]] and [[TranLang III communications module/Legends|TranLang III communications module]]. Cybot Galactica sued for trademark infringement, leading Industrial Automaton to quietly retire the line.

==Description==
The LOM-series was a [[Class three droid/Legends|third-degree]]<ref name="AEG" /> [[Protocol droid/Legends|protocol droid]] manufactured by [[Industrial Automaton/Legends|Industrial Automaton]]. As an effort to challenge [[Cybot Galactica/Legends|Cybot Galactica's]] dominance of the protocol [[Droid/Legends|droid]] market, the LOM-series was designed to appeal to [[Insectoid/Legends|insectoid]] [[Species/Legends|species]]. As such, the droid's head was a generic, [[Insect/Legends|insectlike]] design, with large, prominent [[Photoreceptor/Legends|photoreceptors]] on either side, although they were keyed for the [[Human/Legends|Human]] visual spectrum..<ref name="EGTD" />

[[File:LOM_egtd.png|thumb|left|180px|LOM-series [[:Category:Technical drawing images|schematics]].]]
Industrial Automaton were not content to compete with Cybot Galactica. Instead, they wanted to dethrone the [[3PO-series protocol droid/Legends|3PO-series]] and offer a model that was capable of the same functions but at a lower price point. In an effort to replicate the functionality of the 3PO-series, Industrial Automaton's designers approached equipment suppliers such as [[SyntheTech/Legends|SyntheTech]] and brokered deals with them. Industrial Automaton ended up acquiring identical technical and peripheral components that were used on the 3PO-series,<ref name="EGTD" /> including droid body plating,<ref name="NEGTD" /> resulting in the LOM-series resembling a 3PO unit from the neck down.<ref name="EGTD" />
LOM-series droids were also equipped with [[AA-1 VerboBrain/Legends|AA-1 VerboBrains]] and [[TranLang III communications module/Legends|TranLang III communications modules]] allowing them to communication in millions of [[Language/Legends|languages]]. LOM droids had all the advantages of 3PO units such as their intelligence and cultured manner, and were also less skittish and more prone to acts of altruism and generosity.<ref name="EGTD" />

==History==
In the aftermath of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]],<ref name="NEGTD" /> Industrial Automaton planned to challenge Cybot Galactica's market dominance in the [[Protocol droid/Legends|protocol droid]] field. Realizing that it was unwise to try and compete directly against the 3PO-series, Industrial Automaton tried a different approach. As the 3PO unit was popular with [[Human/Legends|Human]] customers, the company decided to target their model at [[Alien/Legends|alien]] [[Species/Legends|species]]. If their sales projections exceeded their target expectations within two [[Standard year/Legends|years]], Industrial Automaton planned to create a Human-based protocol droid.<ref name="EGTD" />

Designs for the LOM-series protocol droid were swiftly approved, and Industrial Automaton defined a broad target market for their new line. They had seen the disaster that Cybot Galactica had endured with their [[PD-series protocol droid]] and did not want to repeat their competitor's mistake. The LOM-series was designed with [[Insectoid/Legends|insectoid]] [[Species/Legends|species]] in mind, including the [[Brizzit]], [[Verpine/Legends|Verpine]], [[Xi'Dec/Legends|Xi-Dec]], and [[Yam'rii/Legends|Yam'rii]].<ref name="EGTD" />

The LOM-series sold well in its initial, limited release, but plans for future production were put on hold when Cybot Galactica sent an army of copyright [[Lawyer/Legends|attorneys]] after Industrial Automaton. Cybot Galactica was furious at Industrial Automaton's use of trademarked hardware in their new droid, coupled with its clear cosmetic similarity from the neck down to the 3PO-series.<ref name="EGTD" /> They sued for trademark infringement, and violations of noncompetition agreements with companies that supplied components for the 3PO-series.<ref name="NEGTD" /> During the lawsuits, Industrial Automaton suffered a blow to the reputation of the LOM-series when a [[valet]] aboard the ''[[Kuari Princess/Legends|Kuari Princess]]'' became a [[Thief/Legends|thief]] and one of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy's]] most notorious [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunters]].<ref name="EGTD" />

Cybot Galactica was quick to blame shoddy craftsmanship for [[4-LOM/Legends|4-LOM's]] turn to crime, while Industrial Automaton attempted to blame a mysterious programming glitch brought on by the droid interacting with the ''Kuari Princess''{{'s}} shipboard [[Computer/Legends|computer]]. The combination of the lawsuits and the bad publicity from the 4-LOM incident was a public relations nightmare for Industrial Automaton. The LOM-series did not recover<ref name="EGTD" /> and the line was quietly retired.<ref name="NEGTD" />
